backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 (about 262K tokens per step). With only 300 s of training, more optimizer steps usually help a small model. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 so gradient accumulation halves. Leave all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Lower total batch to 2**18

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, which gives 2 accumulation steps per optimizer step. It is a more aggressive step-count increase than 2**18. If the training loop asserts divisibility, it holds, since 2**17 is divisible by 64*2048.
backlog.title: Batch 2**17

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7 so the learning rate decays linearly over the last 70% of the time budget.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.7

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.3 to spend more of the budget at peak LR.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.3

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so the LR does not hit exactly zero at the end of the time budget.
backlog.title: Final LR fraction 0.05

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.02 to remove early instability, particularly if the batch size is also reduced.
backlog.title: Short warmup

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05 for Muon.
backlog.title: Matrix LR 0.05

backlog.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1. Training is short, so less regularization may help.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.1

backlog.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.3 for cautious Muon weight decay.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.3

backlog.spec: Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4.
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.4

backlog.spec: Double UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008.
backlog.title: Unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Halve SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25 for the per-layer scalars.
backlog.title: Scalar LR 0.25

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.9, 0.99), a smoother second-moment estimate for the embeddings and scalars.
backlog.title: Adam beta2 0.99

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 and ASPECT_RATIO = 96, so model_dim = 576. This is rounded to a multiple of HEAD_DIM if the code needs it. The model is shallower, so it runs faster and gets more steps in 300 s.
backlog.title: Depth 6 wider

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 10 with ASPECT_RATIO = 64 (dim 640). Check that VRAM fits. If it OOMs, set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32.
backlog.title: Depth 10

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 7 and ASPECT_RATIO = 73, giving dim 511, which should round to 512 or a multiple of HEAD_DIM. This is a slightly smaller, faster model that gets more steps.
backlog.title: Depth 7

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 to double the number of attention heads. FlashAttention on the A100 handles this efficiently.
backlog.title: Head dim 64

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSL", so full-attention layers are more frequent. The last layer must remain L.
backlog.title: Window pattern SSSSL variants

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSSSSSL" for depth 8. Only the last layer has full attention. This reduces compute per step.
backlog.title: All short windows except last

backlog.spec: If the sliding window size S is computed as half of the context length, change it to a quarter of the context length. This speeds up attention and may cost little quality.
backlog.title: Smaller short window

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP activation (relu squared) with SwiGLU. Use a hidden size of 8/3*dim rounded to a multiple of 64 to keep the parameter count the same.
backlog.title: ReLU squared to SwiGLU

backlog.spec: If the logits use a softcap (such as 15), change it to 30. If there is no softcap, add 30*tanh(logits/30) before the loss.
backlog.title: Logit softcap tuning

backlog.spec: If q and k are RMS-normalised before attention, multiply both by a constant of 1.2 to sharpen attention. Otherwise add the QK norm.
backlog.title: QK norm scale

backlog.spec: Scale the initialization of the output projection of the attention and MLP layers (c_proj) by 0.5. This gives a smaller residual contribution at init and more stable early training.
backlog.title: Untied init scale smaller

backlog.spec: If Muon momentum ramps from 0.85 to 0.95, shorten the ramp to 100 steps, or set the final momentum to 0.97 during the warmdown phase.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup shorter

backlog.spec: Reduce the Muon Newton-Schulz iterations from 5 to 4 if configurable. This saves a little time per step and keeps the rest of the setup unchanged.
backlog.title: Muon Nesterov and ns steps 4

backlog.spec: Make sure the AdamW param groups use fused=True. Also check that no `.item()` syncs occur in the training loop, apart from the periodic logging calls. This is a speed-only change that gives more steps in 300 s.
backlog.title: Disable torch compile overhead: fused optimizer

backlog.spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) before the optimizer step. It stabilises training, particularly at a smaller batch size.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping 1.0

backlog.spec: If the model uses value embeddings on alternating layers, restrict them to the last 3 layers only. This reduces the parameter and optimizer cost.
backlog.title: Value embedding off for fewer layers

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 7 and ASPECT_RATIO = 73 (model dim rounds to 512, 4 heads of 128), and also set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18. Under a fixed 300 s budget, a smaller model with twice as many optimizer steps may do better. Keep everything else unchanged. If gradient accumulation logic depends on TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE / (DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE*seq_len), make sure it still divides evenly (64*2048=131072, so 2 accumulation steps).
backlog.title: Replicate DEPTH 7 / dim 512 with batch 2**18

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown in the LR schedule function with a cosine decay over the final WARMDOWN_RATIO of the time budget: for progress p in the warmdown region, with w=(1-progress)/WARMDOWN_RATIO, multiplier = FINAL_LR_FRAC + (1-FINAL_LR_FRAC)*0.5*(1-cos(pi*w)). Keep the same applicability to Muon momentum and weight decay schedules, if any. No other changes.
backlog.title: Time-based LR warmdown to cosine shape

backlog.spec: Initialize the lm_head weight to zeros (instead of small normal) in init_weights, so the model starts with uniform logits. Keep all other inits. Optionally raise UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.006 to compensate for the zero start.
backlog.title: Weight-tied embeddings off-by-default check: init lm_head to zero

backlog.spec: Change each transformer Block forward to compute attention and MLP in parallel from the same normalized input: x = x + attn(norm(x), ...) + mlp(norm(x)), using a single shared norm call. This reduces sequential depth and kernel launches, giving more steps in 300 s. Leave the rest of the model unchanged.
backlog.title: Parallel attention+MLP blocks

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of model parameters (decay 0.999, updated every step with torch._foreach_lerp_ in no_grad on a copy of the parameters) and swap the EMA weights in just before the final evaluation call, without altering the evaluation call itself. Only do this if the swap happens in the training code before evaluation; keep memory overhead small (a bf16 or fp32 copy of the params is fine).
backlog.title: EMA of weights for evaluation

backlog.spec: For the first 25% of the time budget, train on sequences truncated to half length (reshape each batch of length T to 2B sequences of T/2 tokens, keeping total tokens per step), then switch to full length. This speeds early training via cheaper attention. Use a simple flag in the training loop; compile may recompile once on shape change, which is acceptable since compile time is not counted.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum: short sequences early

backlog.spec: Put the value-embedding parameters in their own Adam param group with learning rate 1.0 (currently they share the EMBEDDING_LR 0.6 group, scaled by model dim). Leave other groups unchanged. Tests whether the value embeddings are under-trained in the short run.
backlog.title: Separate higher LR for value embeddings

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 and MATRIX_LR = 0.06 together, and keep WEIGHT_DECAY at 0.2. A bolder combined change: more steps with a higher Muon learning rate to exploit the short training horizon.
backlog.title: Bigger step: MATRIX_LR 0.06 with batch 2**18

backlog.spec: Simplify the model by deleting the resid_lambdas and x0_lambdas per-layer scalar mixing (set residual forward to a plain x = x + block(x)). Remove the scalar parameter group from the optimizer. This is a simplification; check whether val_bpb is equal or better, which would be a win from less code.
backlog.title: Remove x0 residual mixing and per-layer scalars

incumbent.description: Scale the RMS-normalised queries and keys by 1.2 each in causal self-attention, which sharpens attention logits by 1.44x.
